summary: Afternoon batched workload -> stealth heartbeat suppression + tenant connection fanout causing dedicated pool throughput erosion
description: Customer reports a gradual throughput and p99 latency degradation during their daily afternoon batch window (approx 15:00-16:30 PST). Errors are not outright 5xx but requests are queuing and p99 moves from 420ms -> 2.8s over 40 minutes. Customer is on a dedicated GPU pool and observes retries and occasional fallback to smaller model variants. No new deployment on customer side. Impact: production pipelines slowed, downstream ETL missed SLOs.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer schedule: run 30k short-chat requests over 90m against a pinned dedicated pool route. 2) Observe p50/p99 over time. 3) Compare allocator/heartbeat telemetry and connection counts across tenant sidecars. Note: reproduction tends to occur during platform-wide afternoon load window and is timing-sensitive.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: a background snapshotter sweep in the dedicated pool intermittently delays allocator heartbeats; concurrently one tenant (BrightBench) produces a high short-stream fanout pattern that drives sidecar connection growth and memory churn. Combined effect: allocator reports fewer available slots and autoscaler marks telemetry stale, preventing timely scale-up. Evidence: (1) allocator heartbeats show 10-30s jitter correlated with p99 spikes; (2) sidecar connection counts for tenant spike to >500, unusual for this workload; (3) NVMe IO and snapshotter logs show short bursts overlapping the timeline. We ruled out a new model rollout or customer-side configuration change. Telemetry gaps coincide with autoscaler NO_ACTION decisions. Repro steps attempted in staging produce milder but similar signals when a synthetic fanout client is run concurrently with a snapshot sweep.
comments: 2026-03-10 16:05 - Support (Alicia): Acknowledged to customer, collected request ids and pool id. Requested retention logs for 24h and confirm time window.

2026-03-10 16:40 - SRE (Marcus): Pulled allocator heartbeat timeline and sidecar connection histogram. Noted snapshotter job at 15:08-15:14 on the same host rack. Marking autoscaler/allocator for in-depth review.

2026-03-11 09:12 - Customer (BrightBench - Jenna K): Confirmed batch schedule and provided SDK call traces showing repeated short-lived streams from their aggregator service. Asks for mitigation; business impact is that hourly reports missed thresholds.

2026-03-11 14:23 - Support (Alicia): Temporary mitigation suggested: add client-side connection throttling (cap concurrent streams) and switch to non-batched route for the most latency-sensitive flows. Customer applied client-side throttle; p99 reduced to ~700ms but throughput still below target.

2026-03-12 10:05 - Eng (Marcus): Proposed fix: ensure allocator heartbeats are prioritized over snapshotter IO; add autoscaler heuristic to ignore single-host telemetry blackouts if neighboring hosts report capacity. Drafting PR for small allocator change and autoscaler fallback logic.
resolution: (workaround) Customer applied a client-side concurrency cap and temporarily reduced batch concurrency during the afternoon window; this brought p99 back down to ~700ms. (ongoing fix) Engineering to deploy allocator heartbeat prioritization and autoscaler resilience change in a staged rollout. No permanent platform code change deployed yet.
